transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. My name is Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, well, I guess what brings me in is that my sleep has just gotten really messed up lately. Like, I’ll either stay up half the night with my mind just running and running, or I’ll wake up way too early and feel like I never even rested. 

It's so frustrating. Like the other night, I was just staring at the ceiling at 3 AM thinking about this one spreadsheet at work. I do bookkeeping for this local auto parts place, and honestly, the guy who did the accounts before me left everything in such a mess. I mean, who puts petty cash in the same column as vendor payouts? It makes absolutely no sense. I spent like three hours on Tuesday just trying to reconcile April of last year, and my boss doesn't even care, but it bothers me, you know? I just like things to balance and be where they're supposed to be. 

But yeah, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the sleeping thing. I just wake up feeling completely exhausted.

Besides the work situation, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several different things in your life—like health, family, or finances—most days, even when there's no clear reason to worry?

Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I worry sometimes, sure, but not like all the time about everything. Mostly it's just the stuff at work that gets me going. My sister is always telling me I need to let it go, but she doesn't get it. She's a yoga instructor, so her whole life is just breathing exercises and drinking green juice. She actually tried to get me to go to this retreat with her last month. It was up in the mountains, like two hours away, and they didn't even have cell service. Can you imagine? Just sitting around on a cushion for three days with no phone? I told her there was no way I could leave my cat for that long anyway. Mr. Whiskers gets so stressed when I'm gone. He threw up on my favorite rug the last time I went out of town for a weekend. It's this beautiful Persian rug I found at a thrift store for like fifty bucks, which is a total steal, you know? 

But, um, yeah. I don't really worry about health or family or anything like that. Just regular stuff, I guess.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or having little interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, actually... I have. Lately I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling. It’s hard to explain, but like, even sitting in my own condo that I worked so hard for just makes me want to cry. 

And I worked really, really hard for it, you know? I’ve been saving up since I graduated high school. Getting a mortgage by yourself in your twenties is a total nightmare. The loan officer—this guy named Dan who always wore these really loud novelty ties, like one day he had little golf clubs all over it—he made me submit my bank statements three different times. I mean, I’m a bookkeeper! My statements are completely immaculate. I even color-code my personal expenses. But he still acted like I didn't know what I was doing. It was so insulting. 

I actually painted the living room this really nice sage green right after I moved in, because I read online that green is supposed to be super calming. I got the paint on clearance at the hardware store, too, which was great because the brushes and tape are weirdly expensive. But, um... yeah, I don't know. Even with the green walls and my nice rug, I just sit on the couch and feel so sad. What was the rest of your question? Something about hobbies?
How long have you been feeling this way—this low, empty mood and loss of interest in things you enjoy?

Well, I'd say this depressed, guilty fog has been hanging around for about five months now. It definitely got a lot worse after I bought the condo, though. Which is so weird, right? Because buying a place is supposed to be this huge, exciting milestone. I mean, my mom threw me a little housewarming party and everything. She made these little cucumber sandwiches with the crusts cut off, which is so funny because I haven't eaten a cucumber sandwich since I was like, eight. She used to pack them in my lunchbox when I was in third grade. My teacher that year was Mrs. Gable, and she had this massive collection of snow globes on her desk. Like, dozens of them. I always wondered how she dusted them all, because they were packed so tightly together. You'd think one wrong move and they'd all just shatter. I actually bumped into her at the grocery store a couple years ago, and she didn't even recognize me. But anyway, yeah... about five months of feeling like this.
During these past five months, have you had any thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?

No, no, I haven't wanted to die or anything like that. I just feel so heavy and awful all the time. But no thoughts of hurting myself. I could never do that to Mr. Whiskers anyway. Who would feed him? He's on this very specific diet because he has a sensitive stomach. I have to buy this special food from the vet that costs like forty dollars a bag, which is honestly ridiculous for cat food. But if I give him the regular stuff from the grocery store, he just throws up everywhere. And like I said, he already ruined my Persian rug. I tried everything to get that stain out. I watched all these YouTube tutorials where people mix baking soda and vinegar, and it bubbles up like a science fair volcano. I actually won second place in the science fair when I was in seventh grade. I made a papier-mâché volcano, but I painted it with this glow-in-the-dark paint so it looked like real lava when they turned the lights off in the gymnasium. The kid who won first place just made a potato clock, which I thought was super basic, but his dad was on the PTA so I'm pretty sure it was rigged. But yeah, no, I haven't wanted to hurt myself.
Over these past five months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight—eating more or less than usual?

Yeah, actually. My appetite has been totally off. I keep just skipping dinner entirely, or I'll just sit there eating crackers over my budget notebook because I can't be bothered to cook. Which is a shame, because I have this amazing set of copper-bottom pots that my aunt got me for graduation. She found them at an estate sale, and they were still in the original boxes from like, the 1970s. The lady who owned them before must have never cooked a day in her life. My aunt is always finding stuff like that. She goes to estate sales every single Saturday, rain or shine. She has this whole system where she maps out her route on Friday nights using a physical paper map and a highlighter. I tried telling her about Google Maps, but she refuses to use a smartphone. She still has a flip phone! It takes her like ten minutes just to text me "Happy Birthday." But anyway, yeah, I'm definitely eating less. I noticed my work pants are actually feeling a lot looser than they did a few weeks ago.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or making decisions over these past few months, even with everyday tasks?

Yeah, it's been really bad. I'm a bookkeeper, so my whole job is looking at spreadsheets, and lately, the ones I used to handle easily just blur together. I’ll reread the same row of numbers over and over and still not trust what I entered. Which is so frustrating because I've always been really good with numbers. When I was in high school, I was the treasurer for the drama club. We put on this production of *The Wizard of Oz*, and I had to manage the whole budget for the costumes and sets. We ended up having to make the Tin Man's costume out of actual cardboard boxes and aluminum foil because we ran out of money. The guy playing him, Jason, was sweating so much under all those stage lights that the foil started peeling off in the middle of his solo. He ended up going to college for musical theater, actually. I think he lives in New York now. I always wanted to visit New York, especially during Christmas to see the tree at Rockefeller Center. My cousin went last year and said it was so crowded she couldn't even get a good picture. But yeah, making decisions or just focusing on my work right now feels almost impossible.
Given everything you've been feeling, are you still able to keep up with your job duties and daily responsibilities, or has it become really hard to function at work or at home?

Well, I'm still getting to work, but it's... it's been really hard. I've actually made enough reconciliation mistakes lately that my supervisor had to pull me aside. Which was mortifying, because she's usually so hands-off. Her name is Brenda, and she just had her first grandbaby, a little girl. She shows us pictures every single morning in the breakroom. The baby is cute and all, but Brenda buys her all these extravagant outfits, like tiny little designer dresses that she's just going to spit up on anyway. I remember when my sister had her kids, they basically just lived in onesies for the first year. My sister has three boys, which is just chaos. They're always breaking things. Last Thanksgiving, the middle one threw a football right through the living room window. My dad was so mad, he made them all go sit in the minivan while we finished eating pie. We always have pumpkin and pecan pie, but I'm the only one who actually likes the pecan. I use my grandmother's recipe, which calls for dark corn syrup instead of light. It makes such a huge difference in the flavor. But anyway, yeah, work is a struggle, and outside of work, I'm just... I'm not doing much. I've been avoiding my salsa class and not seeing my friends because I just don't feel like myself. I can't even fake the energy right now.
Have you experienced any unusual beliefs that others might find hard to accept, or seen or heard things that others couldn't, during this time?

No, nothing like that. I haven't been hearing voices or seeing things or anything weird like that. I mean, my apartment gets kind of creaky at night, but that's just because it's an old building. It was built in the 1920s, I think. It still has the original crown molding, which is why I rented it in the first place. I love old architecture. I took an art history class in high school, and our teacher, Mr. Harrison, was obsessed with Art Deco. He used to bring in these huge coffee table books full of pictures of old theaters and hotels in Miami. He actually went to Miami for his honeymoon, which I always thought was a little cliché, but he said they stayed in this amazing boutique hotel right on South Beach. I've never been to Florida. I hate the humidity. My hair gets so frizzy the second there's even a little bit of moisture in the air. I tried this expensive anti-frizz serum that my hairdresser recommended, but it just made my hair look greasy. I ended up giving it to my friend Sarah, who has really thick, curly hair, and she loved it. She's always trying new hair products. She must spend half her paycheck at Sephora. But no, to answer your question, my mind isn't playing tricks on me or anything. It's just... heavy, I guess.

Would you say that, because of how you've been feeling, you're now unable to carry out most of your usual daily activities—like work, household tasks, and self-care—or are you still managing to get through most of them, even if it's difficult?

Well, I mean, I guess I'm still doing the bare minimum, but it's not going well. Like I mentioned, I'm still getting myself to work, but I've been messing up the reconciliations enough that Brenda had to pull me aside and talk to me about it. Which is just... ugh. And she was holding her "World's Best Grandma" mug the whole time, the one with the handle shaped like a teddy bear. I don't know where people find mugs like that. I actually collect vintage Pyrex bowls, the ones with the little flowers or the primary colors? I go to estate sales on the weekends sometimes to find them. Well, I used to. I haven't been doing that lately. I haven't really been doing anything outside of work. Like, I haven't gone to my salsa class in weeks, and I'm totally avoiding my friends. I just... I don't feel like myself, so I don't want to be around anyone. My friend Jessica keeps texting me to go get margaritas, but I just leave her on read. She always wants to go to this place downtown that makes them with jalapeños, which gives me terrible heartburn. I had to start buying those giant bottles of Tums from Costco. Costco is so overwhelming, though, especially on a Saturday. People just leave their carts right in the middle of the aisle while they wait for free samples. It drives me crazy. But yeah, I'm getting through the day, I guess, but I wouldn't say I'm really functioning like I normally do.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to keep up with basic self-care, like showering, grooming, or maintaining your usual hygiene routine, during this time?

I mean, I'm still showering and brushing my teeth and everything, so I guess that part is fine. I haven't let myself go completely. But I definitely haven't been putting in the effort I usually do. Like, I used to do my hair every morning, but lately I just throw it up in a clip. I have this whole collection of claw clips in different tortoise shell patterns. I actually ordered a bunch of them online from this boutique in California because they're supposed to be better for your hair than hair ties. Hair ties give me such a headache if I pull them too tight, especially the ones with the little metal piece on them. I don't even know why they still make those, they just rip your hair out. My mom used to put my hair in these tight French braids when I was little, and I hated it. She'd pull so hard my eyes would water. She was always so particular about how we looked when we went to church. We had to wear these itchy tights and patent leather shoes that gave me blisters. I still have a scar on my heel from a pair of Mary Janes I wore on Easter when I was seven. We went to this huge Easter egg hunt at the park after church, and I couldn't even run because my feet hurt so bad. My brother ended up getting the golden egg that year, which had a five-dollar bill in it. He bought a bunch of Pokémon cards with it. But yeah, I'm still showering and stuff, just... not doing the extra things.

I remember when my sister had her kids, they basically just lived in onesies for the first year. My sister has three boys, which is just chaos. They're always breaking things. We always have pumpkin and pecan pie, but I'm the only one who actually likes the pecan. I use my grandmother's recipe, which calls for dark corn syrup instead of light. It makes such a huge difference in the flavor. But anyway, yeah, work is a struggle, and outside of work, I'm just... I'm not doing much. He used to bring in these huge coffee table books full of pictures of old theaters and hotels in Miami. He actually went to Miami for his honeymoon, which I always thought was a little cliché, but he said they stayed in this amazing boutique hotel right on South Beach. I've never been to Florida. I hate the humidity. My hair gets so frizzy the second there's even a little bit of moisture in the air. I tried this expensive anti-frizz serum that my hairdresser recommended, but it just made my hair look greasy. I ended up giving it to my friend Sarah, who has really thick, curly hair, and she loved it. She's always trying new hair products. She must spend half her paycheck at Sephora. But no, to answer your question, my mind isn't playing tricks on me or anything. It's just... heavy, I guess.

patient.answer: Well, I mean, I guess I'm still doing the bare minimum, but it's not going well. I actually collect vintage Pyrex bowls, the ones with the little flowers or the primary colors? I go to estate sales on the weekends sometimes to find them. Well, I used to. I haven't been doing that lately. I haven't really been doing anything outside of work. Like, I haven't gone to my salsa class in weeks, and I'm totally avoiding my friends. I just... I don't feel like myself, so I don't want to be around anyone. My friend Jessica keeps texting me to go get margaritas, but I just leave her on read. She always wants to go to this place downtown that makes them with jalapeños, which gives me terrible heartburn. I had to start buying those giant bottles of Tums from Costco. Costco is so overwhelming, though, especially on a Saturday. People just leave their carts right in the middle of the aisle while they wait for free samples. It drives me crazy. patient.answer: I mean, I'm still showering and brushing my teeth and everything, so I guess that part is fine. I haven't let myself go completely. But I definitely haven't been putting in the effort I usually do. Like, I used to do my hair every morning, but lately I just throw it up in a clip. I have this whole collection of claw clips in different tortoise shell patterns. I actually ordered a bunch of them online from this boutique in California because they're supposed to be better for your hair than hair ties. Hair ties give me such a headache if I pull them too tight, especially the ones with the little metal piece on them. I don't even know why they still make those, they just rip your hair out. My mom used to put my hair in these tight French braids when I was little, and I hated it. She'd pull so hard my eyes would water. She was always so particular about how we looked when we went to church. We had to wear these itchy tights and patent leather shoes that gave me blisters. I still have a scar on my heel from a pair of Mary Janes I wore on Easter when I was seven. We went to this huge Easter egg hunt at the park after church, and I couldn't even run because my feet hurt so bad. My brother ended up getting the golden egg that year, which had a five-dollar bill in it. He bought a bunch of Pokémon cards with it.
